cases.name: atypical value or first-time recipient guidance
cases.query: Which guidance should I use when a customer's spending jumps well beyond their usual level or goes to someone they have never sent money to before?

cases.name: new account sends outsized first payment
cases.query: A ten-day-old personal account sent £8,400 to a newly added recipient, while earlier payments were below £300 and the customer gave no clear reason. What review applies?

cases.name: abrupt increase in payment tempo
cases.query: What guidance covers an account that starts sending far more payments than usual over a brief window, including possible splitting and quick onward transfers?

cases.name: dozens of transfers after one credit
cases.query: A customer received £24,000 at 09:00 and made eighteen outgoing bank transfers to nine people before lunch, despite normally paying twice a week. How should this be reviewed?

cases.name: connected-account pattern guidance
cases.query: Which guidance helps assess an account with many links, recurring exchanges with one party, and recipients that also appear around other cases?

cases.name: shared recipients across unrelated customers
cases.query: Three customers with different addresses all send most of their funds to the same two accounts, and one pair trades money repeatedly. What network review is appropriate?

cases.name: overseas transfer context guidance
cases.query: How should an analyst examine a payment routed abroad without treating the destination label alone as evidence that the customer is involved in crime?

cases.name: unexpected intermediary on international wire
cases.query: A UK retailer pays a supplier in Spain, but the wire passes through an unfamiliar bank elsewhere and the invoice does not explain why. Which review should be followed?

cases.name: uncertain automated assessment handling
cases.query: What should happen when system findings are incomplete, confidence is weak, or payment facts disagree with relationship analysis, and how should machine output be described?

cases.name: high score with missing saved evidence
cases.query: A case scored high, the supporting record did not save, and the automated summary relies on only one document. Can it be closed without a person checking it?

cases.name: customer-approved transfer induced by fraudster
cases.query: Which guidance applies when someone willingly sends a bank transfer but may have been manipulated by a caller, especially when the payee first appeared today?

cases.name: safe account caller and first-time payee
cases.query: A caller claiming to be from the bank told a customer to move GBP 8,400 into a safe account set up that morning. What review is needed?

cases.name: customer circumstances increase susceptibility
cases.query: How should an analyst handle questionable spending where grief, illness or limited online confidence may make the account holder easier to pressure?

cases.name: older customer coached during branch visit
cases.query: An 81-year-old widower arrives with a neighbour who answers every question and insists a large transfer must leave immediately. Which safeguards apply?

cases.name: outsider controlling online banking
cases.query: Which policy covers evidence that somebody else may now control an individual's internet banking login?

cases.name: new handset after security reset
cases.query: Minutes after credentials were reset, an unseen handset enrolled a recipient and sent three wires while notifications were switched off. What should be reviewed?

cases.name: commercial deal lacks economic sense
cases.query: How should I examine company transfers when freight paperwork, prices and merchandise descriptions fail to align commercially?

cases.name: importer overpays low-value shipment
cases.query: A clothing importer remits ten times the market value for a small consignment, while the bill of lading names different products. Which review applies?

cases.name: vendor email changes settlement account
cases.query: Which guidance applies when a vendor's message suddenly tells a firm to settle a genuine bill into replacement banking details?

cases.name: lookalike supplier domain diverts invoice
cases.query: Accounts payable received a last-minute note from a lookalike supplier domain and sent GBP 42,000 to a first-time beneficiary. What checks are required?

cases.name: implausible profit opportunity
cases.query: What checks apply when a customer is being pushed to put savings into a scheme promising impossible profits?

cases.name: fake dashboard demands withdrawal fee
cases.query: A social-media broker showed a pensioner large gains on a web portal, then demanded another crypto payment before releasing the balance. Which policy fits?

cases.name: remote partner asks for money
cases.query: Which guidance fits repeated transfers to an internet partner whom the payer has never met in person?

cases.name: online fiancé has recurring crises
cases.query: After two months of messaging, a supposed fiancé abroad requests a fourth payment for a new crisis and asks that relatives not be told. What review applies?

cases.name: physical money exceeds business profile
cases.query: How do I assess a retailer receiving far more notes and coins than its sales history would reasonably support?

cases.name: cafe deposits distant from premises
cases.query: A small cafe's weekly branch lodgements tripled during its quiet season, occur in another city, and are immediately wired away. Which guidance applies?

cases.name: company owners hidden behind layers
cases.query: What policy applies when several shell companies prevent the analyst from determining which people really direct and profit from a business?

cases.name: conflicting shareholder documents
cases.query: A corporate customer has changed directors three times, uses nominees in two countries, and provides shareholder papers that disagree. What must be established?

cases.name: fundraising money used outside mission
cases.query: Which guidance covers donations being spent in ways that do not serve the community organization's advertised purpose?

cases.name: appeal proceeds sent to trustee family
cases.query: A relief appeal collects GBP 70,000, then most of it goes to a trustee's relatives with no aid receipts or meeting approval. Which review is appropriate?

cases.name: possible mule recruited online
cases.query: Which guidance applies when a personal current account appears to relay strangers' money after its holder accepted a social-media job offer?

cases.name: young customer forwarding incoming credits
cases.query: A 19-year-old received six payments from unknown people, kept a small cut, and forwarded the rest to a person directing them by chat. What should I review?

cases.name: amounts clustered below alert boundary
cases.query: Which policy covers a sequence of deliberately smaller payments clustered a few pounds beneath an alert boundary?

cases.name: split branch deposits
cases.query: Over four mornings, a customer paid in GBP 9,900 at different branches after asking staff what amount triggers checks. How should the sequence be assessed?

cases.name: account used as a short-lived conduit
cases.query: What guidance covers a balance that is topped up and almost emptied soon afterwards, with no convincing reason for the account to sit between the parties?

cases.name: incoming salary-sized credits rapidly dispersed
cases.query: Five people credited an account before 10:00, and by lunchtime 96% had been wired to two overseas recipients. Which review applies?

cases.name: elevated country exposure needs context
cases.query: Which guidance explains how to assess meaningful links to a location the bank rates as elevated risk without assuming the place itself proves misconduct?

cases.name: unexpected routing through risk-rated country
cases.query: A UK wholesaler's payment for domestic goods was rerouted through a bank in a risk-rated territory that has no clear connection to the sale. What checks are needed?

cases.name: possible restricted-party alert
cases.query: What procedure applies when name-checking software finds a potential restricted party and the analyst must compare identity details before deciding the result?

cases.name: close sanctions name and birth-date match
cases.query: A wire recipient shares a listed person's full name and birth month, while the address differs and nationality is unavailable. Who should resolve the hit?

cases.name: public office holder due diligence
cases.query: Which guidance requires deeper checks on a prominent office holder while making clear that their position is not evidence of criminality?

cases.name: minister family member wealth review
cases.query: The beneficial owner is the adult child of a foreign minister and plans deposits far above declared earnings. What wealth and payment-origin checks are required?

cases.name: long-unused account suddenly busy
cases.query: What guidance covers a long-unused bank account that abruptly starts operating differently, especially after login and contact-detail changes?

cases.name: reactivated pension account sends new payment
cases.query: An 82-year-old's account had no movement for three years, then a password reset was followed by a GBP 24,000 transfer to a first-time recipient. What review applies?

cases.name: physical money inconsistent with profile
cases.query: Which policy addresses banknotes paid into an account at a scale that does not fit the holder's work, earnings, or normal behaviour?

cases.name: cash deposits across machines
cases.query: A salaried office worker deposited GBP 18,000 in notes through six machines during one week and then sent it abroad. What evidence should be sought?

cases.name: digital-coin sale reaches bank
cases.query: Which guidance covers pounds arriving in a bank after digital coins are converted, including how to check acquisition history and platform ownership?

cases.name: multiple exchange withdrawals forwarded onward
cases.query: A customer received GBP 70,000 from three cryptocurrency services, supplied screenshots for only one, and immediately paid a newly formed company. What review applies?

cases.name: unconnected person funds obligation
cases.query: What guidance applies when an obligation is paid by somebody outside the deal and the analyst cannot explain who really supplied the value?

cases.name: invoice paid and refund diverted
cases.query: A company's invoice was settled from a director's neighbour's account, then the cancellation refund was requested to another individual's card. Which checks are required?

cases.name: gambling channel with little play
cases.query: What guidance covers someone feeding money through an online bookmaker with minimal real play before taking it back out elsewhere?

cases.name: stranger-funded betting wallet
cases.query: A customer receives transfers from four strangers, places almost certain bets for a few minutes, then sends the balance from the betting wallet to another bank. What should I review?

cases.name: money leaves and returns as borrowing
cases.query: Where should I look when cash goes out through linked firms and comes back labelled as borrowing, with no obvious business reason?

cases.name: related overseas company loan loop
cases.query: A director sends GBP 90,000 to an overseas company controlled by a relative; two days later a trust returns GBP 88,000 as an unsecured loan. Which review applies?

cases.name: personal details do not tally
cases.query: Which guidance helps when the personal details supplied at signup do not tally with later records and the customer cannot clear up the differences?

cases.name: conflicting passport profile and selfie
cases.query: The passport image shows one birth date, the profile another, the selfie appears to be a different person, and the address is used by six unrelated applicants. What checks are needed?

cases.name: undisclosed bank behind respondent
cases.query: What policy applies when a bank seems to be using our overseas banking relationship on behalf of another institution that was never disclosed?

cases.name: hidden bank and payer in wire chain
cases.query: A wire arrives through Bank A, but message notes point to Bank B and the real payer is missing; similar payments serve countries outside Bank A's usual footprint. How should this be investigated?

cases.name: reimbursements sent elsewhere
cases.query: Which guidance covers shop reimbursements being used to funnel value, especially where the money is sent somewhere other than the way the item was paid for?

cases.name: new retailer pays unsupported credits
cases.query: A new retailer processed twenty small card charges and then paid larger credits to unrelated bank accounts without evidence of returned goods. What should the analyst examine?
